chapter: Chicago: Henderson, Tatum and Roy Eldridge, then New York and the army
title: Roy Eldridge at the Arcadia and Kelly's Stables
summary: Collins worked in Eldridge's big band and small group; at Kelly's Stables he met Leonard Feather and saw the Harlem Highlanders and the pimps and hustlers.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well -- so any way, now I'm going to go back a little farther again. I'm going a little -- let's see, when I went to New York to live I worked with Roy Eldridge at the Areadia Ballroom. He had a big band, a good band.

And we left there, we got a small group and we went to -- we went to Kelly's Stables, which was on 51st Street then I believe. And this is when I first met Leonard Feather, when he first came over. And I -- if I'm not mistaken Leonard was married at that time to a piano player. I'm sure he was.

Yes. I knew his first wife. Yeah. But any way, we went to Kelly's Stables, 51st Street, and let's see who was appearing there then? The Harlem Highlanders. Baby Lawrence, and who almost literally danced up the wall. Oh, they had a tremendous group. Baby Lawrence, they had a guitar player by the name -- his name was Snaggs from Detroit, and another singer, a very talented guy that played bass. His last name was Glover, I don't remember his first name. But so talented.

But we stayed here quite a while, at the Kelly's Stables there. This is when all the pimps and all the hustlers would hang out there. You'd see all the prostitutes. They would bring -- the madams would bring all the girls in and set them around the table. And I could tell you some stories about Jackie Gill, our old favorite. You remember Jackie Gill? This is when I met Jackie Gill. He was one of the boys.
